research_report:
EVENT AND BASELINES — At the cutoff (02:00 EDT), American Bitcoin had scheduled its Q2 2026 release before the August 3 regular session; the 08:30 EDT/12:30 UTC call is not part of the trigger [S1]. The first complete official release or filing is the only eligible package. Q1 issuer-defined baselines were $62.118m revenue, $29.598m cost of revenue, 52.35% implied mining gross margin, 817 BTC mined, approximately $36,200 cost per BTC, 7,021 BTC held including 3,090 pledged, 663 pre-split satoshis per share, 28.1 EH/s owned and 25.0 EH/s operational after April 22, and 14.1 J/TH operational efficiency [S2][S3]. Cost per BTC excludes depreciation, G&A, financing and capex; owned EH/s is not operational EH/s; gross holdings are not unrestricted liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA does not remove the BTC fair-value loss and therefore is not a clean mining-profit measure. The July 1-for-15 reverse split makes the sequential SPS comparator 9,945, calculated as 663 × 15; approximately 11,100 would only be a scenario assuming the public production yardstick is retained with no intervening sales or denominator changes [S4]. Neither SPS figure is a spillover metric. Management supplied no numerical Q2 guidance.

PUBLIC OPERATING BENCHMARK — Published April, May and June FPPS hashprice averages were $33.92, $36.60 and $30.37 per PH/s/day, with BTC hashprice of 0.00046128, 0.00046887 and 0.00048032 BTC per PH/s/day [S5][S6][S7]. Applying 21.9 EH/s through April 21 and 25.0 EH/s thereafter gives a definition-close but imperfect Q2 yardstick of about $74.4m and 1,040 BTC; assuming 25.0 EH/s for all April gives about $76.6m and 1,070 BTC. Uptime, curtailment, pool fees and realized-price conventions prevent treating this as exact. It establishes that a low/mid-$70m revenue result would largely reflect already-public network economics. Dynamic analyst snapshots disagreed and had split-sensitive EPS definitions, so EPS consensus was not locked.

CAUSAL SCREEN — IREN was the nearest operating analogue but failed the trade gate. ABTC's ASICs are exclusively hosted at Hut 8 with pass-through costs and ABTC retains BTC; IREN owns its infrastructure, generally liquidates mined BTC and is actively displacing mining capacity for AI Cloud. Its March quarter already contained $111.2m mining revenue, $33.6m AI Cloud revenue and substantial mining-equipment impairment [S8]. ABTC cannot reveal IREN-specific power prices, curtailment, ASIC removals or AI deployment, while shared BTC/hashprice inputs were already public. MSTR failed because Strategy's value transmission is BTC price, financing, preferred obligations and BTC per diluted share—not mining economics—and it had disclosed 846,000 BTC at June 30 versus ABTC's 7,021 at March 31 [S9]. COIN failed because ABTC discloses no material trading-volume, custody-fee, USDC, derivatives or payments linkage, and Coinbase's own Q2 disclosure was scheduled four days earlier [S10]. Same-direction movement would therefore be common crypto-factor correlation, not evidence that ABTC caused candidate cash-flow revisions.

PRICE-IMPACT CALIBRATION — No candidate survived, so no directional percentage or no-action band was fabricated. The exact MSTRUSDT and COINUSDT Binance equity perpetuals launched only in February 2026 and trade 24/7 [S11]; IRENUSDT launched June 3, after IREN's latest earnings [S12]. No exact candidate instrument had a qualifying candidate-own BMO earnings sample sufficient to estimate separate upside, downside and ordinary in-line distributions. Context only: using Nasdaq underlying-equity closes, IREN moved from $48.65 to $46.37 (-4.7%) on November 14, 2025 after ABTC reported a broadly positive Q3 package, and from $44.03 to $44.24 (+0.5%) on February 26, 2026 after another positive Q4 package [S13][S14][S15]. These observations were excluded from calibration because they predate the exact IRENUSDT contract, number only two, have the same positive issuer direction but opposite candidate signs, and are contaminated by BTC/macro and concurrent earnings. ABTC's May 6, 2026 package was also excluded because its SEC acceptance at 16:20:18 EDT made it AMC, not BMO [S3]. Substituting underlying equity, AMC events or generic volatility would violate the required candidate-own BMO calibration.

DEBATE ADJUDICATION — The financial analyst initially proposed retaining IREN conditionally; the industry analyst and impact critic rejected it on model mismatch, pre-observed common inputs and absent exact-instrument calibration. After receiving the same conflict packet, the financial analyst revised to rejection and withdrew all proposed percentage gates. All three ultimately rejected IREN, MSTR and COIN and agreed that six directional tiers could not honestly be locked. The empty candidate list is therefore an affirmative no-trade conclusion, not a fallback caused by a strong condition failing. All ranked ledger questions are resolved: the package definitions and public operating yardstick are locked, every proposed transmission path was tested, and insufficient calibration caused candidate removal as required.
